reviewNotes: Real photographs for every public article that had no image or only a drawn illustration. New files come from Wikimedia Commons under CC BY, CC BY-SA or CC0 licences (listed per file in the media attribution); each candidate was checked visually against its article before selection.

Where no authentic image of the subject exists or no freely licensed photo was found, a clearly labelled contextual photograph is used: Imam Muhammad bin Saud (At-Turaif, the seat of government he established), Imam Turki bin Abdullah (the modern mosque named after him, existing media 13), Talal Maddah (Al-Muftaha village, whose theatre bears his name). Souq Okaz is left without an image: no freely licensed photograph of the site was found and an unrelated Taif photo would mislead.

Existing approved media are reused where they already show the subject: Riyadh city (10), Diriyah Governorate (7), Masmak Palace (14), Unification of Saudi Arabia (15, archival portrait of King Abdulaziz, 1945).
Alt text describes what is visible; it never claims more than the Commons file description supports.
